pages.text:
The Gas Turbine Array burns fuel straight to FE, with no boiler in between.
- A hollow 3x3 tube, 5 to 9 long, lying on its side. Pressure Glass can replace any casing except the corners.
- One end is the **intake**: it needs open air in front of its centre. The other end is the **exhaust**.
- Feed fuel into an input port. Naphtha, Light Oil, Ethanol, Hydrogen and Biogas burn; Heavy Oil, Creosote and Biodiesel don't.
- From standstill at full throttle it takes about 10 seconds to spool up (lubricant shortens that), making less FE until it's up to speed. Smaller throttle changes follow quickly. It coasts down over about 4 seconds.

# Output
Each mB of fuel gives about 1.5× the FE a Fuel Burner and Thermoelectric Plant would make from it, scaled by how hot the fuel burns.
| Fuel | FE per mB |
| Naphtha | {fe:600} |
| Light Oil | {fe:313} |
| Ethanol | {fe:338} |
| Hydrogen | {fe:90} |
| Biogas | {fe:62} |
It burns up to 2,500 HU of fuel per tick per block of length: a 9-long array handles 22,500 HU/t, about {fe:33750} FE/t on Naphtha. Heavy Oil or Seed Oil in a lubricant port adds 8% and spools it up faster. Its output cap is its full-throttle lubricated output, and it holds 400 ticks of that.

# Combined cycle
Set a heat port on the exhaust end. It gives off a quarter of the fuel's heat at half its burn temperature (Naphtha: 600°C). Put a Steam Boiler Array against it and run the steam through a Steam Turbine Array: together they make about 2× what a Fuel Burner would.
Unused exhaust vents into the air.
# Throttle
Set the Redstone tab to Throttle: signal 1–15 runs fuel flow from 7% to 100%. Throttle mode reads the signal strength; a Throttle Lever sets it directly. If the fuel runs out it flames out, then relights 1 second after fuel returns.
A Gas Output port (named Flue Gas) gives off Carbon Dioxide while it burns carbon fuels: see Carbon Capture.
